newsitem.title: USA: Campaign 'watchdog' said tethered to tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Campaign 'watchdog' said tethered to tobacco.

text.p: A campaign watchdog group, which recently released a study on campaign contributions by trial lawyers, was created by a public relations firm hired by Philip Morris Cos and secretly conducted the study for the company, the Washington Post reported in Monday editions.

The Post said it had documents proving that the supposedly independent and nonpartisan group, Contributions Watch, was created by a lobbying firm, State Affairs Co., that worked with Philip Morris, the maker of Marlboro cigarettes, and a major Washington law firm that represents the tobacco industry.

The connections among the various groups represent a new frontier in lobbying, the Post said, saying creation of a nonprofit watchdog to generate press coverage helpful to the client's cause was a new twist on lobbying practices.
State Affairs specializes in state-level public relations and grassroots lobbying work, and Philip Morris was its biggest client this year.

The company's partners, Charles Francis and John Davis, confirmed to the paper Friday that the study detailing hundreds of millions in campaign contributions by lawyers was done for Philip Morros and other tobacco clients, but said this did not undermine the study's results.
Trial lawyers and the tobacco giants are at odds over efforts to change state laws to shield tobacco firms from liability suits.
